newsitem.title: UK: Northern Ireland still open for business - minister.
newsitem.headline: Northern Ireland still open for business - minister.

text.p: Northern Ireland is still open for business despite the images of violence and destruction over the last year, Northern Irish economy minister Baroness Denton said on Friday.
"Our economy has grown and is in good health. Independent surveys are pointing to improved growth this year," Denton said in a statement.
Economists say the Northern Ireland economy withstood two decades of guerrilla war and began to flourish anew with the twin IRA and Loyalist ceasefires of 1994.
But signs of a return to all-out sectarian warfare augur badly for Investment and are likely to hit tourism, the most vulnerable and potentially lucrative sector, they say.

Denton said, however, that Northern Ireland business had shown before that it would not be stopped by violence and there had been many positive stories in every business sector to offset the negative.

Unemployment, at 9.6 percent, is at its lowest level for over 16 years while manufacturing output has increased at more than three times the national average since the end of the first quarter of last year, she said.

Trade with the Irish Republic continues to show healthy growth while the region's Industrial Development Board has backed investments by externally-owned companies of nearly 600 million pounds ($984 million) since the Irish Republican Army ended a 17-month ceasefire in February 1996.

"Our ports and airports have been busier than ever before, carrying additional passengers and cargo, bearing out recent independent economic surveys which predicted a strong rise in trade and exports," Denton said.
Even tourism, one of the sectors most vulnerable to violence, enjoyed a good year in 1996, Denton said.
"Forecast figures for 1996 suggest that total visitors will be up by about 13 percent on 1994, the year prior to the ceasefires," she said.
Denton said the business community had worked tirelessly over the years to bring economic success to Northern Ireland and their hard work and commitment was now paying dividends.

"Government and business will continue that commitment to the people of Northern Ireland to ensure as far as possible that the prosperity we are enjoying now is not diminished," she said. ($1=.6097 Pound)
